items.rationale: The model has no memory outside the text in the current call; a new session starts empty, so the program must load a saved record or the model must ask. Option a shows M1 (the model remembers on its own); d shows M2 (a bigger window carries memory across sessions).
Call 1 sends 1,100; call 2 sends 3,100; call 3 sends 5,100; call 4 sends 7,100. The total is 16,400. Counting each result only once (7,100) shows that results are not re-sent (M3).
Load only what this student needs: one short record. Everything loaded is re-sent and paid for on every call, and manuals belong in retrieval, not session start. Option d shows M1.

items.rationale: The model keeps nothing between calls, so the program re-sends the full list, and input tokens are billed on each call. Cost grows with steps times window size. A wrong answer that says the model must think harder or the longer text is slower to read shows M3.

Chunks cut out of a manual lose which machine they belong to; putting the machine name and heading in each chunk (or filtering by machine) lets retrieval and the model tell them apart. A larger window or more chunks adds tokens without fixing the ambiguity, and M2 is the idea that a larger window fixes it.
